notes: fit: equivalent = same job, similar model; partial = same job, different model or missing features; gap = no managed OCI equivalent in this map.
complexity is a planning heuristic for effort: low, medium or high. It is not an estimate.
Every OCI Terraform type here is tested against the OCI provider schema. Service facts link to Oracle documentation; check them for the features you use.

source_type_notes.aws_alb: Alias of aws_lb; documented on the aws_lb page.
source_type_notes.azurerm_app_service: Removed in azurerm 4.0; still found in older code.
source_type_notes.azurerm_function_app: Removed in azurerm 4.0; still found in older code.
source_type_notes.azurerm_postgresql_server: Single Server, retired; still found in older code.
source_type_notes.azurerm_mysql_server: Single Server, retired; still found in older code.

differences: Flexible shapes size OCPUs and memory separately; an x86 OCPU is one physical core with two threads.
Machine images are not portable as-is; rebuild them or import the disk as a custom image.
compute-vm.migration: Recreate from infrastructure code with an OCI image, or import the disk image as a custom image.

differences: Scaling is metric- or schedule-based on an instance pool built from an instance configuration.
Lifecycle hooks and warm pools need a different design.
autoscaling-group.migration: Define an instance configuration from the launch template, then an instance pool and autoscaling policy.

sources.azure: App Service, Container Apps, Container Instances

differences: No built-in request-based autoscaling, revisions or traffic splitting; run several instances behind a load balancer, or use OKE when the app needs them.
Platform features such as deployment slots, managed TLS and built-in sign-in need explicit replacements.
container-service.migration: Push the same container image to OCIR and run it as container instances behind a load balancer.

alternatives.when: The app needs autoscaling, rolling deploys or many services.

differences: Cloud-specific ingress annotations, storage classes, load balancer annotations and pod identity integrations must be replaced.
Pods reach OCI services through OKE workload identity.
kubernetes.migration: Redeploy manifests or Helm charts with OCI ingress, storage classes and registry; move persistent volumes with a backup tool.

differences: Functions are container images built with the Fn Project FDKs; handler signatures change.
Check timeout, memory and concurrency limits against each handler.
Triggers differ: HTTP through API Gateway, OCI events through the Events service, schedules through Resource Scheduler.
serverless-functions.migration: Port each handler to the FDK for the same language and reconnect its triggers.

differences: Authentication uses auth tokens or instance principals; update CI credentials and pull secrets.
container-registry.migration: Re-tag and push images; update CI pipelines and pull secrets.

sources.aws: Amazon RDS or Aurora for PostgreSQL
sources.gcp: Cloud SQL or AlloyDB for PostgreSQL

differences: Check the major version and every extension you use against the supported list.
Superuser access and some parameters are restricted, as on other managed services.
managed-postgres.migration: pg_dump and pg_restore for small databases; logical replication for a low-downtime cutover.

alternatives.when: You want relational, JSON and vector data in one Autonomous AI Database.

sources.aws: Amazon RDS or Aurora for MySQL/MariaDB

differences: Check the MySQL version and InnoDB-only assumptions; MariaDB-specific features need review.
managed-mysql.migration: MySQL Shell dump and load utilities; inbound replication for a low-downtime cutover.

sources.azure: Oracle Database@Azure or Oracle on VMs
sources.gcp: Oracle Database@Google Cloud or Oracle on VMs

oci.name: Autonomous AI Database or Base Database Service

differences: Autonomous AI Database manages patching and tuning; check options, features and database links you depend on.
managed-oracle.migration: OCI Database Migration or Zero Downtime Migration; Data Pump for smaller databases.

sources.azure: Azure SQL Database or Managed Instance

oci.name: SQL Server on OCI Compute (license-included Marketplace images)

differences: No managed SQL Server service in this map: the team owns patching, backups and high availability on Compute.
Azure SQL Database features such as serverless tiers and elastic pools have no equivalent.
managed-sqlserver.migration: Backup and restore, or log shipping, to SQL Server on Compute; consider a move to PostgreSQL only with a tested application change.

sources.aws: Amazon RDS or Aurora (engine not detected)

oci.name: Depends on the engine: OCI Database with PostgreSQL, MySQL HeatWave or Autonomous AI Database

differences: The scanner could not read the engine; check the template or module inputs and re-run.
managed-relational.migration: Decide after the engine is known.

sources.azure: Cosmos DB Table or Cassandra API, Table Storage

differences: Different API and SDK: plan code changes in the data access layer.
Check secondary indexes, TTL, change streams, transactions and multi-region tables against what you use.
key-value-nosql.migration: Export to JSON or Parquet in Object Storage and load; dual-write during the cutover.

oci.name: Autonomous AI Database JSON with the MongoDB API

differences: The MongoDB API covers common operations; check the commands and operators your driver uses.
Change feeds and real-time listeners need a different design.
Cosmos DB's NoSQL API and Firestore SDKs need code changes.
document-db.migration: mongodump and mongorestore, or a JSON export and import.

alternatives.when: Access is by key and simple queries at high scale.

differences: Check engine version, cluster mode and the commands you use. Memcached users need a client change.
cache-redis.migration: Usually rebuilt empty and warmed by the application; export an RDB file only if the cache holds data you cannot recompute.

differences: SQL dialect, functions and loading tools differ; rewrite queries and pipelines.
Pricing is by compute and storage rather than by data scanned.
data-warehouse.migration: Export to Parquet or CSV in Object Storage, then load with DBMS_CLOUD.

differences: Gremlin and openCypher queries need translating to SQL property graph queries.
graph-db.migration: Export vertices and edges to CSV, load as tables, define the property graph.

oci.name: Autonomous AI Database (Globally Distributed Autonomous AI Database for sharding)

differences: Interleaved tables, commit timestamps and the SQL dialect do not translate directly.
Decide whether the app needs global distribution at all before choosing the target.
distributed-sql.migration: Schema redesign and an export/load through Object Storage.

differences: S3 SDKs work through the Amazon S3 Compatibility API with Customer Secret Keys and an OCI endpoint; check the operations you use.
Azure Blob and Cloud Storage SDKs need code changes to the OCI SDK or the S3 API.
Bucket policies become IAM policies; object events come from the Events service.
object-storage.migration: rclone or OCI CLI bulk copy; the Data Transfer service for very large volumes.

sources.aws: S3 static website hosting, Amplify Hosting

oci.name: A web container or Object Storage behind a load balancer or CDN

differences: No managed static-site service with routing rules, preview environments and managed TLS in this map.
static-site.migration: Serve the build output from a small web server container behind the load balancer, with a CDN in front if needed.

differences: File Storage serves NFS; SMB shares from Azure Files need another approach.
file-storage.migration: rsync or a parallel copy tool over NFS.

differences: Performance is set with volume performance units per GB.
block-storage.migration: Copy data at the file system level, or import disk images.

differences: Route tables, security lists and gateways are separate resources; subnets are regional and span availability domains.
Use a service gateway to reach OCI services without the internet.
vpc-network.migration: Recreate the address plan in Terraform; avoid CIDR overlap with networks you will connect.

differences: Public or private is a property of the subnet.

oci.name: Network security groups and security lists

differences: Network security groups attach to VNICs; security lists apply to whole subnets. Rules that reference other groups become NSG-to-NSG rules.
Tag-based GCP firewall targets need NSGs instead.
firewall-rules.migration: Translate each rule; review for over-broad sources while doing it.

differences: Outbound IP changes; tell partners who allow-list your egress address.
Listeners, path routing and certificates are configured differently; certificates come from OCI Certificates or are uploaded.
load-balancer-l7.migration: Recreate listeners, backend sets and health checks; test routing rules before DNS cutover.

differences: Routes, authorizers and usage plans become deployment specifications.
Full API management features such as developer portals and monetisation are narrower.
api-gateway.migration: Translate routes from the OpenAPI definition; re-create authorizers as JWT or function-based authentication.

oci.name: Cloudflare@OCI, or Web Application Acceleration at the load balancer

differences: OCI has no first-party global CDN in this map. Cloudflare services are sold and billed through OCI as Cloudflare@OCI (price list parts B112540 to B112555, checked 2026-10-21).
Web Application Acceleration adds caching and compression at an OCI load balancer, not at a global edge.
cdn.migration: Recreate cache rules and origins in the chosen CDN; cut over by DNS.

differences: Provider-specific alias and routing-policy records become steering policies or plain records.
dns.migration: Export the zone file, import it, lower TTLs before cutover, then switch name servers.

differences: Managed rule sets and rule syntax differ; re-create rules and run them in detection mode first.
waf.migration: Translate rules, run in detection mode against real traffic, then enforce.

differences: Connections terminate on a dynamic routing gateway (DRG).
vpn.migration: Build the new tunnels in parallel before moving traffic.

differences: Provisioning involves a partner or colocation; lead times apply.
dedicated-interconnect.migration: Order early; run VPN in the meantime.

differences: Similar model (visibility timeout, dead-letter queue) with a different API and SDK.
Check FIFO, sessions and ordering guarantees you rely on.
message-queue.migration: Drain the old queue while producers switch; keep consumers idempotent.

differences: Fan-out to email, HTTPS, Functions, SMS and other endpoints; message filtering and durable pull subscriptions differ.
Where consumers pull, use OCI Queue or Streaming instead.
pub-sub-topic.migration: Recreate topics and subscriptions; switch publishers, then retire old subscriptions.

differences: Kafka-compatible API; Kinesis client library consumers and enhanced fan-out need rework.
Check retention and throughput limits.
event-streaming.migration: Dual-publish during cutover, then move consumers.

sources.azure: Event Hubs Kafka endpoint or self-managed Kafka

differences: Check Kafka version, authentication method and connector support.
managed-kafka.migration: MirrorMaker 2 replication, then move consumers and producers.

differences: Events reacts to OCI service events. Custom application event buses map to Notifications, Queue or Streaming.
event-routing.migration: Split rules into OCI service events (Events) and application events (Queue, Notifications or Streaming).

sources.azure: Logic Apps or Functions timer triggers

differences: Cron schedules invoke a function in detached mode without a payload.
Scheduled container jobs can run as Kubernetes CronJobs on OKE.
scheduler.migration: Recreate each schedule; move job parameters into function configuration.

oci.name: Oracle Integration, or orchestration in code

differences: State machine and workflow definitions do not translate automatically.
Airflow DAGs from Cloud Composer can run on self-managed Airflow on OKE.
workflow-orchestration.migration: Rebuild flows in Oracle Integration, or move orchestration into application code or Airflow.

sources.azure: Entra External ID or Azure AD B2C

differences: OIDC, OAuth 2.0 and SAML are supported; the app changes issuer, client settings and token claims.
Password hashes are not portable: plan resets or migrate users at next sign-in.
Hosted sign-in pages, triggers and custom flows need replacements.
identity-users.migration: Bulk-import users, run old and new sign-in in parallel, migrate users as they sign in.

oci.name: IAM policies, dynamic groups and resource principals

differences: Policies are statements scoped to compartments.
Workloads authenticate as instance or resource principals rather than attached roles or service accounts.
iam-roles.migration: Rewrite each permission as least-privilege policy statements per compartment.

differences: Keys do not move between clouds; data encrypted with the old keys is re-encrypted as it is copied.
kms.migration: Create new keys; re-encrypt data during transfer.

differences: Applications read secrets with the OCI SDK and a resource or instance principal.
Plain configuration parameters belong in application configuration rather than a vault.
secrets.migration: Re-create secrets by hand or script without printing values; rotate them after the move.

differences: Provider-managed public certificates are not exportable; issue new ones for the OCI endpoints.
certificates.migration: Issue or import certificates before cutover.

differences: Query syntax differs; Logging Analytics covers advanced search and dashboards.
logging.migration: Point agents and services at new log groups; keep old logs where retention rules require.

differences: Alarm conditions use Monitoring Query Language (MQL).
metrics-alarms.migration: Translate each alarm; send them to a Notifications topic.

differences: OpenTelemetry instrumentation moves most easily; vendor-specific agents need replacing.
apm-tracing.migration: Switch exporters to the APM endpoint.

differences: Send by SMTP or API; set up sender domain authentication (SPF and DKIM) before cutover.
email.migration: Verify the domain and warm up sending volume gradually.

differences: The model catalogue differs: choose an available model and re-run your quality evaluation.
On-demand use needs no Terraform resource; dedicated clusters and endpoints do.
Check model availability in your region.
gen-ai.migration: Swap the client and model, run the evaluation gate, then switch traffic. Unit cost: founder-value-ai.

differences: Pipelines, feature stores and SDK-specific training jobs need rework; framework code (PyTorch, scikit-learn) moves as is.
ml-platform.migration: Move model artefacts and training code; rebuild pipelines and deployments.

oci.name: OCI Data Flow (Apache Spark) and OCI Data Integration

differences: Plain Spark jobs move with configuration changes; Glue DynamicFrames, Data Factory pipelines and Databricks features need rewriting.
spark-etl.migration: Move data to Object Storage, then port jobs one at a time with output comparison.

sources.aws: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink

oci.name: OCI Data Flow (Spark), after a rewrite

differences: No managed Beam or Flink runner in this map: rewrite in Spark or run the engine yourself on OKE.
beam-pipelines.migration: Rewrite and validate outputs side by side.

differences: Azure AI Search has its own API and skills; moving from it is a rewrite to OpenSearch queries or vector search in Autonomous AI Database.
search.migration: Reindex from the source of truth, or snapshot and restore between OpenSearch versions.

sources.aws: Session Manager, EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint

differences: Sessions are time-limited SSH or port forwarding.
bastion.migration: Recreate access paths; remove public SSH.

differences: Budgets alert; they do not stop spending. Use quotas to bound resource use.
budget.migration: Create a budget per compartment before the first deploy.

sources.aws: AWS SDK calls in application code
sources.azure: Azure SDK calls in application code
sources.gcp: Google Cloud SDK calls in application code

oci.name: OCI SDK, the S3 Compatibility API, or a portable library

differences: Each call site needs review; the package name alone does not show which services the code uses.
cloud-sdk.migration: List call sites, wrap them behind an interface, then switch the implementation.

oci.name: Same container on OKE or Container Instances, or the managed service named in the finding

differences: Runs unchanged in containers; moving to a managed service is optional and is listed as an opportunity.
self-hosted.migration: Move the container and its volumes; consider the managed alternative.
